name: Celestica
exchange: NYSE (also listed on the Toronto Stock Exchange)
description: Celestica designs and builds hardware for other companies' brands. About 74% of 2025 revenue came from its Connectivity and Cloud Solutions (CCS) segment, which makes network switches, optical systems, racks, servers and storage for cloud and AI data centers, mostly for hyperscalers; the rest is Advanced Technology Solutions (ATS), classic contract manufacturing for aerospace and defense, industrial, health-tech and semiconductor-equipment customers. Customers place orders for specific products and Celestica earns a thin manufacturing margin, plus a better margin where it also designs the product (its Hardware Platform Solutions line, an ODM business, which was 41% of 2025 revenue). It is very concentrated: three customers were 32%, 14% and 12% of 2025 revenue and the top ten 79%. Revenue rose 28% to $12.4 billion in 2025 and 83% to $5.83 billion in the third quarter of 2026 as AI data-center build-outs ramped.

sub.name: Data-center networking, servers, optics and cooling

hq.note: 5140 Yonge Street, Suite 1900 (FY2025 10-K Item 1). About 75% of 2025 revenue was produced in Asia and about 20% in North America.

employees.note: Permanent and temporary (contract) employees worldwide (FY2025 10-K Item 1); 26,865 a year earlier.

businessLines.name: Connectivity and Cloud Solutions (CCS)
businessLines.how: Sells finished networking, optical, rack, server and storage systems built to a cloud customer's specification on program contracts; margin is thin on pure build-to-print work and higher on HPS where Celestica designs the product, but each program needs R&D and working-capital investment.
businessLines.description: Communications end market (networking switches, optical systems, data-center racks, mostly for hyperscalers and cloud/AI service providers) and Enterprise end market (servers and storage). Includes the Hardware Platform Solutions (HPS) ODM business, where Celestica designs or co-designs the product. From 2026 the 10-Q splits CCS revenue into Networking and Compute & Storage.

operatingProfit.note: Share is of the two segments' combined income ($927.0M); FY2024 $478.5M (7.4%)

businessLines.name: Advanced Technology Solutions (ATS)
businessLines.how: Manufactures customers' regulated, lower-volume products (defense electronics, medical devices, industrial controls, chip-equipment subsystems) under long-running manufacturing programs, earning a manufacturing and supply-chain margin per unit built.
businessLines.description: Aerospace and defense, industrial (automation, controls, test and measurement, energy and power efficiency products), HealthTech (surgical instruments, diagnostic imaging, patient monitoring) and capital equipment (semiconductor equipment and subsystems). Traditional EMS: Celestica does not generally co-design the products.

brands.name: Hardware Platform Solutions (HPS)
brands.share: 41% of FY2025 company revenue (29% in 2024, 21% in 2023)

brands.name: Celestica Enterprise end market (servers and storage)
ATS end markets: Aerospace and Defense, Industrial, HealthTech, Capital Equipment
brands.share: 26% of FY2025 revenue combined; the split among the four is not given in the passages read
